extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent owners/agents practicing in ex parte reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on handling responses, amendments, petitions, timing, and examiner actions after a final rejection in ex parte reexamination proceedings. Covers when amendments will be entered, time extensions, petition practice, and examiner notification duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rejection ends unrestricted prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a final rejection that is not premature has been entered in a reexamination proceeding, the patent owner no longer has any right to unrestricted further prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration of amendments submitted after final rejection and prior to, or with, the appeal will be governed by the strict standards of 37 CFR 1.116; consideration of amendments submitted after appeal will be governed by 37 CFR 41.33. There is no right to refile under 37 CFR 1.53(b) or 1.53(d), nor to file a request for continued examination under 37 CFR 1.114.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop and present all issues before final action
rubrics_metrics.description: Both the examiner and the patent owner should identify and develop all issues prior to the final Office action, including presentation of evidence under 37 CFR 1.131(a) and 1.132.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because substantial patent rights will be at issue with no opportunity to refile, parties must present prior art, arguments, and evidence before final rejection. The MPEP emphasizes full development of the record pre-final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition under 37 CFR 1.181 for premature or improper final or refusal to enter amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner believes a final rejection is improper or premature, or that an amendment complying with 37 CFR 1.116 was improperly refused entry, the owner may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.181 requesting withdrawal of the final rejection or entry of the amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 1.181 petition must be filed within the time period for filing a notice of appeal. Filing a 1.181 petition does not toll the time period for filing a notice of appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory response period and automatic two-month extension for first response
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory period for response to a final rejection in a reexamination proceeding will normally be two (2) months. In ex parte reexamination proceedings the time period is automatically extended by two months if the response is the first response after the final rejection and a notice of appeal has not yet been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any timely first response after final (even informal or unsigned) triggers the automatic two-month extension; the advisory action PTOL-467 will inform the patent owner of the extension. The total reply period may not be extended past six months from the date of final rejection. The automatic two-month extension conforms to the Patent Law Treaty (PLT); additional 'no cause' extensions are not available for patent-owner-requested or Director-ordered reexaminations. Extensions beyond two months require a showing of sufficient cause under 37 CFR 1.550(c)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner entitled to examiner ruling on timely after-final response before appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner is entitled to know the examiner's ruling on a timely response filed after final rejection before being required to file a notice of appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification of the examiner's ruling should reach the patent owner with sufficient time for the owner to consider and act; the examiner's advisory action should extend the period for response appropriately so the owner can act on the ruling. See cited case Theodore Groz & Sohne & Ernst Bechert Nadelfabrik KG v. Quigg.

rubrics_metrics.name: No right to amend, add, or reinstate claims after final without meeting entry standards
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner cannot, as a matter of right, amend any finally rejected claims, add new claims after a final rejection, or reinstate previously canceled claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry of an amendment filed after final rejection and prior to an appeal requires a showing under 37 CFR 1.116(b) and will be evaluated by the examiner, except where the amendment merely cancels claims, adopts examiner suggestions, removes issues for appeal, or requires only a cursory review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to 1.116(b) showing for after-final amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Some after-final amendments need not be supported by the 1.116(b) showing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, an amendment that merely cancels claims, adopts examiner's suggestions, removes issues for appeal, or in some other way requires only a cursory review by the examiner can be entered without the substantive 1.116(b) showing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for entry of after-final amendments touching the merits
rubrics_metrics.description: For an amendment touching the merits of the patent under reexamination, the patent owner must provide a showing of good and sufficient reasons why the amendment is necessary and was not earlier presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatively, an amendment may be entered if (A) the total effect is to cancel claims or comply with form requirements set forth in a previous Office action or present rejected claims in better form for consideration on appeal. Examiners should evaluate whether the amendment puts claims in patentable condition or reduces/simplifies issues on appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: First proposed amendment after final to be given full consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The first proposed amendment after final action in a reexamination proceeding will be given sufficient consideration to determine whether it places all the claims in condition where they are patentable and/or whether the issues on appeal are reduced or simplified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the proposed amendment is not entered in its entirety, the examiner will briefly explain reasons for not entering it. If the claims as amended present a new issue requiring further consideration or search, the examiner should identify the new issue and briefly explain why a new search or consideration is necessary. The patent owner should be notified if certain portions of the amendment would be entered if filed separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second and subsequent after-final amendments limited in consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Any second or subsequent amendment after final will be considered only to the extent that it removes issues for appeal or puts a claim in an obvious patentable condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits serial after-final amendment practice to filings that directly simplify or resolve appealable issues or make claims patentable without reopening broad prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: No MPEP §2266.01/2266.02 cure practice after final; use advisory action for defects/omissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice of giving the patent owner a time period to supply an omission (MPEP §2266.01) or notifying defects via PTOL-475/PTO-2311 and setting time for correction (MPEP §2266.02) does not apply after a final Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a bona fide response filed after final omission/inadvertence lacks some point necessary to fully respond, the examiner should not issue a notice of failure to fully respond; instead issue an advisory Office action (e.g., PTOL-467) explaining the omission. Likewise, a defective (informal) response after final should not be handled by PTOL-475/PTO-2311 but by advisory action explaining the defect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality and consequence of canceled claims in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents undergoing reexamination cannot become abandoned and cannot be refiled, and the holding of claims unpatentable and canceled in a certificate is absolutely final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because canceled claims are final, it is appropriate for the examiner to consider the feasibility of entering amendments touching the merits after final rejection or after appeal where the patent owner shows why the amendments are necessary and why they were not earlier presented.
